cited_details.statement: [introduce a learned state estimator](https://elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf) that infers the pose of an object being manipulated by a multi-fingered hand using only proprioceptive feedback.

The broader **DexYCB** benchmark provides a standardized capture protocol and ground-truth annotations for 2D/3D hand pose and 6D object pose estimation during grasping, enabling fair comparison of such estimators in manufacturing-relevant pick-and-handover scenarios [DexYCB](https://dex-ycb.github.io/).

Oller, Berenson, and Fazeli [propose a tactile-driven framework](https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf) that combines passive compliance modeling with an explicit notion of *extrinsic contact modes* to manipulate a grasped object against the environment (e.g., pivoting on a tabletop).

introduce **TacGNN**, a hierarchical graph neural network that learns a tactile-driven dynamics model for an anthropomorphic hand operating without vision ([TacGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.00736)).

The OpenAI study ["Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.00177) established that a five-fingered humanoid hand can learn to reorient a block to arbitrary target poses from vision alone, using large-scale distributed RL in simulation and domain randomization to bridge the sim-to-real gap.

earlier showed that **RL with tactile features** can acquire regrasping skills on a passively compliant hand and generalize to novel objects [van Hoof et al., 2015](https://users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf), foreshadowing the role of tactile sensing in fine manipulation.

study **on-policy learning robust to irreversible events** such as object slipping, combining a visual RL policy with a low-level tactile reactive controller that intervenes to prevent drop [Falco et al., 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.08927).

Roldan Sanchez, Wang, and Cordova Bulens propose a **hierarchical RL scheme that uses Davenport chained rotations** to represent in-hand object orientation, thereby reducing the effective action dimensionality for a Shadow-hand-like platform [Roldan Sanchez et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00795).

Separately, the synergy-space DRL approach learns a low-dimensional manifold of natural hand poses from human demonstrations and trains the policy in that space, achieving an 88.38% success rate on relocation tasks compared to a substantially lower rate for the unstructured baseline [Anthropomorphic Hand via DRL, 2021](https://doi.org/10.3390/s21165301).
introduce **H-InDex**, which augments visual RL with hand-informed representations learned by predicting future hand state [H-InDex, 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01404).

The **DexArt** benchmark extends the evaluation setting to articulated objects (drawers, boxes, faucets) and provides a reproducible testbed for measuring generalization across object instances [DexArt, CVPR 2023](https://cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341).

Finally, Li, Donato, Lomonaco, and Falotico study **continual policy distillation** so that soft-hand controllers can be updated to new tasks without catastrophic forgetting of previously acquired skills [Continual Policy Distillation, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04219).

combine a small number of human-collected demonstrations with model-free deep RL to acquire a broad set of visuomotor skills for a simulated hand [Zhu et al., RSS 2018](https://doi.org/10.15607/rss.2018.xiv.009).

**DexMV** learns dexterous manipulation from monocular human videos by first estimating hand and object poses with an off-the-shelf tracker, then re-targeting the human trajectory to a simulated robot hand, and finally training an RL policy in simulation on the re-targeted trajectories [DexMV, 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877).
